title: Remove Location from a Photo Copy Before Sharing on iPhone
description: To remove location from a photo you share, export a separate copy with location retention disabled, then inspect the exported file’s metadata.
direct: To remove location from a photo you share, export a separate copy with location retention disabled, then inspect the exported file’s metadata. This removes a metadata clue; visible landmarks and other details in the picture can still reveal where it was taken.
figureAlt: A location pin stays out of a photo sharing envelope while the original remains archived.

cards.choice.heading: Check the file you will send
cards.choice.body: The original in Photos and an exported copy can have different metadata. Inspect the exact file attached to your message or upload, rather than assuming a setting changed every copy already in another app.
sections.explain.heading: Native sharing is another option
sections.explain.body: Apple also offers location controls when sharing photos. Check the available Options in the share sheet for your iOS version and destination. A recipient may still infer location from signs, buildings or faces. Metadata removal is therefore a useful file-handling step rather than an anonymity guarantee.
sections.practice.heading: Be aware of conversion changes
sections.practice.body: Our app supports choosing whether to keep capture date and location, but conversion can also change format or presentation. JPEG uses compression and replaces transparency with white; choose a supported output that suits the recipient. The first three successful photo conversions are free; each photo in a batch counts, with more requiring purchase. Space Sheep Studio develops PhotoFix. This guide makes no claim about stripping every possible private field or altering copies already shared.

steps.step-1.text: Open the photo in PhotoFix: HDR to Normal Photos on iPhone and choose an appropriate supported conversion.
steps.step-2.text: Disable location retention for the export. Decide separately whether to retain capture date and keep the original untouched.
steps.step-3.text: Save a new copy, inspect its location information in a trusted photo/file inspector, and share that verified file.
